description: Pin bumps for the kit (docs/maintenance.md, section 5.3). The pins that follow an upstream release carry a
`# renovate:` comment in pins.toml, which the regex manager below reads; `xdrcheck pins latest` reads the same
comments, so the nightly job and this bot see one list. One pull request per move; each must pass
`make verify-static` (xdrcheck pins check), and some need hand steps the pull request body names. The
conformance driver directories are historical columns pinned on purpose and are never bumped.

customManagers.description: pins.toml entries annotated with `# renovate: datasource=... depName=... [versioning=...] [extractVersion=...]`

packageRules.description: In go.mod files only the modules pins.toml names move; everything else follows them through go mod tidy.
A Go module moves in pins.toml and in go/go.mod and lint/go.mod together.

prBodyNotes: A stellar-core move is not only a version: also move `[stellar_core]` commit, deb_url, deb_sha256, binary_sha256, image and test_image, then `make fetch` and `make verify-static`. A new protocol is the upgrade procedure in docs/maintenance.md, section 5.
Also move `[stellar_xdr_definitions]` commit, and `rust.stellar_xdr` with it. A new tag usually means a new protocol: docs/maintenance.md, section 5.

Crates are also pinned in Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock (root, or contracts/ for soroban-sdk): update both, rebuild, and run `make verify-static` and `make test`. Move `[conformance.columns]` only when adding a new driver column.

An SDK move adds a conformance column: a new drivers/<sdk>/<version> directory with its lock file, the version in `[conformance.columns]` and a column in drivers/sets.d/<family>.toml (docs/maintenance.md, section 5.3). Review the nightly canary report first.
Also move `[pipelines.stellar_etl]` commit (and go_toolchain if its go.mod changed), then `make lint-stellar-etl`.
